- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overweights short-term momentum; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day after day 10 to reflect diminishing momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 10-day rolling average of past 30 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67), model exhibits erratic behavior; use weighted average of 3-day sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
